source.title: Lieutenancies Act 1997, Schedule 1
source.licence: Crown copyright. Contains public sector information licensed under the Open Government Licence v3.0.

method: All 33 London, all 63 English unitary and all 36 metropolitan records reviewed against Schedule 1, including the legislation incorporated by paragraph 2(c). The 164 other English district records retain existing county council membership, with the applicable schedule provision recorded. Scotland, Wales and Northern Ireland retain 65 explained blanks. Stockton is the sole English blank because the schedule splits it between two counties. GSS codes identify registry records and do not appear in the Act. This reference is maintained independently of the registry builder.

Cheshire.quote: Cheshire East, Cheshire West and Chester, and, Halton and Warrington

Dorset.quote: Bournemouth, Christchurch and Poole and Dorset

Durham.quote: Durham, Darlington, Hartlepool and so much of Stockton-on-Tees as lies north of the line for the time being of the centre of the River Tees

The East Riding of Yorkshire.quote: The East Riding of Yorkshire and Kingston upon Hull (City of)

East Sussex.quote: East Sussex and Brighton and Hove

Lincolnshire.quote: Lincolnshire, North Lincolnshire and North East Lincolnshire

North Yorkshire.quote: North Yorkshire, Middlesbrough, Redcar and Cleveland, York and so much of Stockton-on-Tees as lies south of the line for the time being of the centre of the River Tees

Somerset.quote: Somerset, Bath and North East Somerset and North Somerset.

London.quote: Greater London (excluding the City of London);

OtherEnglishCounties.quote: any other areas in England which are counties for the purposes of the Local Government Act 1972.

City.quote: The City of London shall be treated as a county for the purposes of sections 5 and 6.

Scilly.quote: The Isles of Scilly shall be treated as part of the county of Cornwall for the purposes of this Act.

Wales.quote: The counties in Wales for the purposes of this Act are the preserved counties, that is to say, the counties in Wales as they stood immediately before the passing of the Local Government (Wales) Act 1994 (but subject to any redrawing of their boundaries by or under that Act or the Local Government Act 1972).

Scotland.quote: the cities of Aberdeen, Dundee, Edinburgh and Glasgow;

Scope.quote: The provisions of this Schedule identify the areas which constitute counties in England, counties in Wales or areas in Scotland for the purposes of the lieutenancies in Great Britain.

rutland.title: The Leicestershire (City of Leicester and District of Rutland) (Structural Change) Order 1996

herefordshire.title: The Hereford and Worcester (Structural, Boundary and Electoral Changes) Order 1996

wight.title: The Isle of Wight (Structural Change) Order 1994

evidence.quote: A new county shall be constituted comprising the area of Rutland and shall be named the county of Rutland.

Rutland.note: The order creates a county comprising the Rutland district. Paragraph 2(c) therefore applies.

evidence.quote: A new county shall be constituted comprising the area of the new district of Herefordshire and shall be named the county of Herefordshire.

Herefordshire.note: The order creates a county comprising the new Herefordshire district. Paragraph 2(c) therefore applies.

evidence.quote: New counties of North West Somerset, Bath and North East Somerset, South Gloucestershire and the City of Bristol shall be constituted and shall comprise the district areas of North West Somerset, Bath and North East Somerset, South Gloucestershire and the City of Bristol respectively.

Bristol.note: The statutory county name is City of Bristol. Unlike the other new Avon counties, it is not reassigned by paragraph 3 of Schedule 1.

evidence.quote: “Berkshire” means the Royal County of Berkshire and “the County Council” means the council of that county;

The County Council shall be wound up and dissolved and the functions of that council in relation to each Berkshire district shall, subject to the following provisions of this Part and to any other relevant provision, be transferred to the council of that district.
the three coroners' districts in the County of Berkshire
the one consisting of the Borough of Reading;
the one consisting of the District of Newbury; and
the one consisting of the Boroughs of Bracknell Forest, Slough and Windsor and Maidenhead and the District of Wokingham.
On 1 April 1998 the name of the Council was changed from Newbury District Council to West Berkshire District Council:

Berkshire.note: The 1996 order abolishes the county council, not Berkshire. The 1998 order confirms the six district areas within the county. The 2002 Act confirms the West Berkshire name. The county label omits the honorific Royal County of.

evidence.quote: “Cornwall”, except in the definition of “the Cornwall council” and the second mention of those words in article 3(2), means the county of Cornwall;
On and after 1st April 2009 the Cornwall council shall be the sole principal authority for Cornwall.

For the purposes of enactments relating to local government, there shall be a new district, whose area shall be co-terminous with that of Cornwall; and the name of that new district shall be Cornwall.

Cornwall.note: The order retains the county council as sole principal authority and creates a district with the same area as the county.

evidence.quote: “Northumberland”, except in the definition of “the Northumberland council” and the second mention of those words in article 3(2), means the county of Northumberland;
On and after 1st April 2009 the Northumberland council shall be the sole principal authority for Northumberland.

For the purposes of enactments relating to local government, there shall be a new district, whose area shall be co-terminous with that of Northumberland; and the name of that new district shall be Northumberland.

Northumberland.note: The order retains the county council as sole principal authority and creates a district with the same area as the county.

evidence.quote: “the Island” means the county of Isle of Wight,
the Island council shall be the sole principal council for the Island
As from the reorganisation date, the Island council shall be renamed the Isle of Wight Council.

Isle of Wight.note: The county council becomes the sole principal council for the county and is renamed the Isle of Wight Council. The county remains in existence.
